questions.prompt: What is electric current?
options: Charge passing a point per unit time
questions.explanation: I = Q/t; one ampere is one coulomb per second.

questions.prompt: Which unit measures electric charge?
questions.explanation: Charge Q is measured in coulombs, C.

questions.prompt: In a metal wire, which particles drift to carry charge?
questions.explanation: Mobile electrons carry charge through a metal.

questions.prompt: Compared with conventional current, electron drift in a metal is…
questions.explanation: Conventional current is defined in the direction of positive charge motion.

questions.prompt: A lamp has a steady current entering and leaving it. What is used up?
options: Electrical energy is transferred; charge is conserved.
questions.explanation: Charge is not consumed; the lamp transfers electrical energy to other stores and pathways.

questions.prompt: A steady current of 0.2 A flows for 30 s. How much charge passes? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Q = It = 0.2 × 30. Result: 6 C.

questions.prompt: A steady current of 0.5 A flows for 60 s. How much charge passes? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Q = It = 0.5 × 60. Result: 30 C.

questions.prompt: A steady current of 1.5 A flows for 20 s. How much charge passes? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Q = It = 1.5 × 20. Result: 30 C.

questions.prompt: A steady current of 2 A flows for 45 s. How much charge passes? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Q = It = 2 × 45. Result: 90 C.

questions.prompt: A steady current of 3 A flows for 120 s. How much charge passes? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Q = It = 3 × 120. Result: 360 C.

questions.prompt: Potential difference is energy transferred per…
questions.explanation: V = E/Q, with J/C equivalent to volts.

questions.prompt: Which relationship applies to an ohmic resistor at constant temperature?
questions.explanation: Potential difference is proportional to current for an ohmic resistor at fixed temperature.

questions.prompt: Which unit measures resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms, Ω.

questions.prompt: The voltage across a fixed ohmic resistor doubles. Its current…
questions.explanation: I = V/R and R is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Why specify constant temperature when investigating an ohmic metal resistor?
options: Voltage is always zero when hot.
Temperature changes can change its resistance.
questions.explanation: Heating a metal usually increases its resistance, changing the current–voltage relationship.

questions.prompt: An ohmic 12 Ω resistor is connected across 6 V. Find the current. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: I = V/R = 6/12. Result: 0.5 A.

questions.prompt: An ohmic 8 Ω resistor is connected across 12 V. Find the current. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: I = V/R = 12/8. Result: 1.5 A.

questions.prompt: An ohmic 3 Ω resistor is connected across 9 V. Find the current. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: I = V/R = 9/3. Result: 3 A.

questions.prompt: An ohmic 20 Ω resistor is connected across 4 V. Find the current. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: I = V/R = 4/20. Result: 0.2 A.

questions.prompt: An ohmic 25 Ω resistor is connected across 10 V. Find the current. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: I = V/R = 10/25. Result: 0.4 A.

questions.prompt: Components connected in series have the same…
questions.explanation: There is one conducting path, so the same current passes through each series component.

questions.prompt: Parallel branches share the same…
questions.explanation: Each branch is connected between the same two circuit nodes.

questions.prompt: Adding an identical resistor in parallel makes the total resistance…
questions.explanation: Another branch adds a conducting path; two equal parallel resistors have half the resistance of one.

questions.prompt: Which expression gives electrical power?
questions.explanation: Voltage is energy per charge and current is charge per time, so VI is energy per time.

questions.prompt: Two unequal resistors are in parallel across an ideal battery. The smaller resistor carries…
questions.explanation: Both see the same V, so I = V/R is larger for the smaller resistance.

questions.prompt: A device operates at 6 V and 0.4 A. What is its power? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: P = VI = 6 × 0.4. Result: 2.4 W.

questions.prompt: A device operates at 12 V and 2 A. What is its power? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: P = VI = 12 × 2. Result: 24 W.

questions.prompt: A device operates at 9 V and 0.5 A. What is its power? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: P = VI = 9 × 0.5. Result: 4.5 W.

questions.prompt: A device operates at 230 V and 8 A. What is its power? Give the closest value.
A device operates at 5 V and 0.2 A. What is its power? Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: P = VI = 5 × 0.2. Result: 1 W.

questions.prompt: Two positive point charges exert forces that are…
questions.explanation: Like-sign charges repel; unlike-sign charges attract.

questions.prompt: Coulomb’s law uses which separation?
questions.explanation: The point-charge formula uses the separation of the charge locations in SI units.

questions.prompt: Doubling the separation of unchanged point charges makes the force…
questions.explanation: F is proportional to 1/r².

questions.prompt: Reversing the sign of one charge, keeping magnitudes and separation fixed, changes…
questions.explanation: The product of signs determines attraction or repulsion; absolute magnitudes determine force size.

questions.prompt: Electric field arrows around a positive point charge point…
options: Nowhere because positive charges have no field
questions.explanation: Field direction is the force direction on a small positive test charge; this is an extension idea.

questions.prompt: Two point charges have magnitudes 1 μC and 2 μC, separated by 0.5 m in vacuum. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹. Find the force magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert μC to C, then F = k|q₁q₂|/r². Result: 0.0719 N.

questions.prompt: Two point charges have magnitudes 2 μC and 3 μC, separated by 0.3 m in vacuum. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹. Find the force magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert μC to C, then F = k|q₁q₂|/r². Result: 0.599 N.

questions.prompt: Two point charges have magnitudes 4 μC and 1 μC, separated by 0.2 m in vacuum. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹. Find the force magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert μC to C, then F = k|q₁q₂|/r². Result: 0.899 N.

questions.prompt: Two point charges have magnitudes 3 μC and 5 μC, separated by 0.6 m in vacuum. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹. Find the force magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert μC to C, then F = k|q₁q₂|/r². Result: 0.375 N.

questions.prompt: Two point charges have magnitudes 2 μC and 2 μC, separated by 1 m in vacuum. Use k = 8.99 × 10⁹. Find the force magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert μC to C, then F = k|q₁q₂|/r². Result: 0.036 N.

questions.prompt: A fuse or overcurrent breaker primarily protects wiring against…
questions.explanation: Excessive current can overheat wiring; overcurrent protection disconnects it.

questions.prompt: An RCD compares…
options: Outgoing live and returning neutral currents
Current and elapsed time in every case
questions.explanation: A sufficient imbalance indicates current returning by another path.

questions.prompt: What is the role of protective earthing on a suitable metal-cased appliance?
options: Provide a protective path if the case becomes live
Carry the normal operating current in every circuit
questions.explanation: Earthing works with suitable protection to reduce danger after a fault.

questions.prompt: A balanced overload can fail to trip a plain RCD because…
options: RCDs detect only heat in every wire
Live and neutral currents can still be equal
questions.explanation: A plain RCD detects imbalance; separate overcurrent protection is needed.

questions.prompt: Before a real mains socket is changed, the appropriate approach is…
options: Qualified work with supply isolated and verified safe
Rely on a wall switch alone
Use the virtual model as authorisation to work live
questions.explanation: The simulation teaches principles, not live-mains working procedures.

questions.prompt: A simplified 30 mA RCD test has live current 8.08 A and neutral current 8 A. What is predicted?
options: No trip from this imbalance alone.
The currents must add before comparison.
The RCD must also detect every balanced overload.
questions.explanation: Compare |I_live − I_neutral| = 80 mA with 30 mA. Real devices also have trip-time specifications.

questions.prompt: A simplified 30 mA RCD test has live current 5.02 A and neutral current 5 A. What is predicted?
options: The currents must add before comparison.
No trip from this imbalance alone.
The RCD must also detect every balanced overload.
questions.explanation: Compare |I_live − I_neutral| = 20 mA with 30 mA. Real devices also have trip-time specifications.

questions.prompt: A simplified 30 mA RCD test has live current 3.05 A and neutral current 3 A. What is predicted?
options: No trip from this imbalance alone.
The currents must add before comparison.
The RCD must also detect every balanced overload.
questions.explanation: Compare |I_live − I_neutral| = 50 mA with 30 mA. Real devices also have trip-time specifications.

questions.prompt: A simplified 30 mA RCD test has live current 2.01 A and neutral current 2 A. What is predicted?
options: No trip from this imbalance alone.
The currents must add before comparison.
The RCD must also detect every balanced overload.
questions.explanation: Compare |I_live − I_neutral| = 10 mA with 30 mA. Real devices also have trip-time specifications.

questions.prompt: A simplified 30 mA RCD test has live current 10.04 A and neutral current 10 A. What is predicted?
options: No trip from this imbalance alone.
The currents must add before comparison.
The RCD must also detect every balanced overload.
questions.explanation: Compare |I_live − I_neutral| = 40 mA with 30 mA. Real devices also have trip-time specifications.

questions.prompt: Which is a unit of electrical energy used on bills?
questions.explanation: kWh is power multiplied by time; it measures energy.

questions.prompt: A tariff of 0.30 currency units/kWh gives the cost by multiplying the tariff by…
questions.explanation: Cost = energy × tariff, before any extra charges.

questions.prompt: Halving use time at fixed power makes energy consumption…
questions.explanation: E = Pt, so energy is directly proportional to time at fixed power.

questions.prompt: Raising the electricity tariff while using the same appliance for the same time changes…
options: Cost but not electrical energy use
questions.explanation: Tariff is a price per energy unit, not a physical operating condition.

questions.prompt: Why is a 2 kW appliance not necessarily more costly per day than a 1 kW appliance?
options: All devices use equal energy daily
Tariffs depend only on device colour
questions.explanation: Compare Pt for the full daily use, not power alone.

questions.prompt: A 2000 W appliance runs at constant power for 3 h. Find its energy consumption. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert watts to kilowatts, then E = 2.0 × 3. Result: 6 kWh.

questions.prompt: A 100 W appliance runs at constant power for 5 h. Find its energy consumption. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert watts to kilowatts, then E = 0.1 × 5. Result: 0.5 kWh.

questions.prompt: A 1500 W appliance runs at constant power for 2 h. Find its energy consumption. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert watts to kilowatts, then E = 1.5 × 2. Result: 3 kWh.

questions.prompt: A 750 W appliance runs at constant power for 4 h. Find its energy consumption. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert watts to kilowatts, then E = 0.75 × 4. Result: 3 kWh.

questions.prompt: A 3000 W appliance runs at constant power for 0.5 h. Find its energy consumption. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: Convert watts to kilowatts, then E = 3.0 × 0.5. Result: 1.5 kWh.
